events.text: The main brownstone structure was completed.
events.subject: self

events.text: The three brick structures at 60–64 Stone Street date to 1836.
events.subject: self
events.quote: which date to 1836 and were built as commercial stores

events.text: The New York Cotton Exchange was founded.
events.subject: other
events.quote: The New York Cotton Exchange , founded in 1870

events.text: The New York Cotton Exchange began occupying the building.
events.subject: self

events.text: The building served as the headquarters of W.R. Grace and Company until the early 1910s.
events.subject: self
events.quote: served as the headquarters of W.R . Grace and Company until the early 1910s

events.text: The structures were purchased by the India House.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1914 , the structures were purchased by the India House

events.text: The three Stone Street stores began being gradually combined with the brownstone structure.
events.subject: self
events.quote: being gradually combined with the brownstone structure between the 1870s and 1910s

events.text: The combining of the three Stone Street stores with the brownstone structure ended.
events.subject: self

events.text: The building was designated a city landmark by the LPC.
events.subject: self
events.object: New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission
events.quote: designated a city landmark by the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission ( LPC ) in 1965

events.text: The building was added to the National Register of Historic Places.
events.subject: self
events.quote: added to the National Register of Historic Places ( NRHP ) in 1972

events.text: The building became a National Historic Landmark.
events.subject: self
events.quote: became a National Historic Landmark in 1977

events.text: The Stone Street Historic District was designated by the LPC.
events.subject: other

events.text: The Stone Street Historic District was designated by the NRHP.
